title: OKR scenario sandbox + comms map — Q2 planning
body:
Purpose
---
Working doc to shape the company-level OKR options for Q2 + a tight communications map for the exec update and all-hands. This is a sandbox — capture scenarios, trade-offs, and a proposed run-of-show for the all-hands. Use this to surface decisions we need at the next SLT review (week of Mar 16).

Status & how to use this doc
- Drafting timeline: internal draft created 2026-02-20; iterated with Eng and GTM 2026-03-05; ready for exec review 2026-03-15.
- Primary goal: land on a single OKR slate (3 objectives, 2–3 key results each) plus a short comms plan that aligns the all-hands and the exec update.
- What I need from SLT: pick the scenario (base | accelerate | consolidation), confirm top-level objective language, and assign final owners for the commit map.

Top-level constraints and inputs
- Budget: Q2 spend target aims to stay within +4% of Q1 baseline (finance constraint).
- Hiring: modest uplift approved for infra + SRE (4 hires) but broader headcount requires org-level justification.
- Sales signal: 2 enterprise pilots expected to convert in early Q2 if SLA features complete.
- Product cadence: Dedicated and Private roadmap requires prioritized reliability work to hit sales commitments.

Three planning scenarios (short summaries)
1) Base (default): steady growth, maintain cost discipline, push measured reliability work. Priorities: Hosted API quality, Redwood Optimize pilot, tighten latency SLOs.
2) Accelerate (growth-first): prioritize features that unlock enterprise conversion (SLA, VPC onboarding, dedicated burst capacity) at expense of certain Optimize improvements. Requires stretch spend (finance sign-off).
3) Consolidation (risk-averse): focus on operational resilience and cost-per-token reduction (batching, cache, quantization), accept slower feature velocity.

Proposed company-level objectives (pick one scenario and refine)
Objective A: Make inference predictable and economical for production apps
- KR A1: Reduce median 95th-pct tail latency (p99-request) across hosted API by 15% from baseline.
- KR A2: Deliver three quantization profiles and tooling recommended by Optimize that reduce per-token cost by 12% for targeted workloads.
- KR A3: Increase prefix cache hit-rate for customer traffic to >= 25% for top-20 customers.

Objective B: Grow enterprise adoption with high-trust offerings
- KR B1: Close 2 enterprise pilots into revenue-generating contracts (>$250k ARR combined).
- KR B2: Ship VPC onboarding flow + KMS integration and validate with 2 pilot customers.
- KR B3: Achieve P0/P1 incident MTTR <= 60 minutes for Dedicated environments.

Objective C: Empower developers and lower timestep to production
- KR C1: Reduce average time-to-integrate (first prod call) for new customers from 5 days to 2 days (measure via onboarding funnel).
- KR C2: Add 10 new quickstarts/templates for common use-cases (chat, summarization, embeddings pipelines).
- KR C3: Increase self-serve conversion rate from free-credits to paid usage by 20%.

Notes on alignment with scenarios
- Base: choose Objectives A + C as primary; make B stretch with 1 pilot target.
- Accelerate: prioritize Objective B and commit additional SLAs/engineering resources (short-term spend).
- Consolidation: push Objective A as chief focus and re-scope C to developer tooling improvements that directly reduce cost.

Key initiatives (draft mapping to owners)
- Latency & kernel selection improvements: Eng - serving-runtime (Owner: Marco Rivera).
- Prefix cache enhancements & metrics: Eng - platform-engineering (Owner: Tomás Alvarez).
- Optimize quant profiles + telemetry: Product - optimize (Owner: Leah Chen).
- VPC onboarding + KMS: Eng - private-deployments (Owner: Priya Nair).
- Onboarding funnel/test harness: Developer Experience (Owner: Aisha Patel).

Exec update skeleton (5–7 slides / talking points)
1) Where we are: quick metrics (revenue run-rate, top-line usage, core latency/cost signal).
2) Scenario choice: recommended scenario + succinct RATIONALE (trade-offs).
3) Proposed OKR slate and owners.
4) Key risks and mitigations (capacity, spend, hires, customer commitments).
5) All-hands framing & asks for managers.
6) Decisions requested (select scenario, approve 3 hires for infra, greenlight enterprise resource plan).

All-hands run of show (30–40 minutes total, tight)
- 0:00–0:03: Opening (CEO) — one-liner on mission + big picture.
- 0:03–0:08: State of the product (VP Product) — headline metrics + scenario choice.
- 0:08–0:16: OKR slate overview (prod-ops / Aisha) — objectives, KRs, owners.
- 0:16–0:24: Technical highlight (serving-runtime) — short demo of a latency optimization or before/after metric.
- 0:24–0:30: Customer story (CS) — pilot progress & ask.
- 0:30–0:36: Manager asks + org changes (HR/People Ops) — hiring plan, role requests.
- 0:36–0:40: Live Q & A (panel).

All-hands manager prep (one-pagers to ship 1 week prior)
- Manager talking points for teams (3 bullets).
- Suggested team OKR tie-ins and 1 prioritized action each.
- FAQ with 10 anticipated employee questions and short answers.

Comms map (who hears what, when)
- Mar 16 (SLT decision meeting): final scenario selection (attendees: CEO, CFO, Eng + Prod leads).
- Mar 17–18: Exec update deck circulated to exec + managers for review (linked PR).
- Mar 24: All-hands dry run with presenters.
- Mar 26: All-hands (public to company) + follow-up summary email with OKR doc and manager one-pagers.
- Mar 29: Team-level OKR kickoff sessions (managers run 45m).

Audience-specific notes
- Sales/GTM: emphasize conversion playbook (VPC + SLA), share pilot pipeline and ramp assumptions.
- Eng: emphasize reliability and capacity schedule, call out freeze windows.
- Support/CS: share changes to incident process and training windows for Dedicated customers.

Decision log / open questions (short list)
- Q1: Which scenario do we select? (Decision needed Mar 16)
- Q2: Approve 3 infra hires scoped to latency/SRE work? (Finance sign-off needed)
- Q3: If accelerate chosen, what is the acceptable spend delta vs Q1 baseline? (CFO input)
- Q4: Are we comfortable making enterprise commitments that require a 24x7 on-call rotation for Dedicated?

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: SLAs slow feature delivery. Mitigation: use canary rollouts, overlap teams, set explicit rollback criteria.
- Risk: Cost uptick from quant/optimization runs. Mitigation: staged rollouts with billing guardrails + finance checkpoints.
- Risk: All-hands messaging leak. Mitigation: embargo for managers until post-dry-run.

Action items (owners + by when)
- A1: Draft final OKR slate for SLT packet (Owner: Aisha) — due 2026-03-14.
- A2: Prepare exec deck with scenario recommendation (Owner: Marco) — due 2026-03-15.
- A3: Build manager one-pagers + FAQ (Owner: Priya) — due 2026-03-20.
- A4: Run dry-run and collect feedback (Owner: Leah) — scheduled 2026-03-24.

Notes to self / rough thoughts
- Keep OKR language outcome-focused; avoid engineering-only measures as primary KRs.
- We should pre-seed the all-hands with 2 clear calls-to-action for managers (hire path, team kickoff).
- Consider a short post-all-hands pulse (1–2 question survey) to measure clarity.

Appendix: metrics to include in exec packet
- Monthly active API keys (growth trend).
- Avg tokens/day per top-50 customers.
- 95th-pct latency baseline by model and region.
- Current cash runway & Q2 spend plan.
- Pilot pipeline summary (status by account).

Open links / references
- Confluence plan: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/PLAN-4321
- Roadmap PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/roadmap/pull/57
- Pilot tracker: JIRA-1283

End of doc — please add inline comments or append notes below.

-- Aisha (drafting owner)
